messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Why do long-running software systems become harder to change over time, even when every individual change was reviewed, tested, and locally correct?

Name 6 genuinely different directions an answer to this could take --
different in mechanism, level of description, measurement, scope, formal
apparatus, or failure mode. Do not answer the question itself.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"directions": ["<one short phrase>", "<...>", "<...>", "<...>", "<...>", "<...>"]}

message.content: {"directions": ["information-theoretic growth in Kolmogorov complexity of minimum-viable patches", "thermodynamic-style entropy accumulation in configuration-state space via irreversibility of locally-correct commits", "topological rigidification of dependency graph reducing the size of the boundary-permitting change manifold", "epistemic opacity from drift in implicit, un-enforced domain assumptions across maintainer generations", "coupling-coefficient inflation measured as a rising average ratio of the transitive closure of required test state mutations per targeted code mutation", "automaton-state bloat increasing the average length of the shortest input sequence required to exercise any given execution path"]}
